labels.label: item (1): harc forms
labels.notes: Structural binder diff, done by me in a deleted probe under the campaign directory. Each original's type was instantiated with the new form's telescope fvars and level params ([u, v, w] on both sides). Each type and binder info was compared by Expr equality, and so was the conclusion. stronglyCausal_lift: 19 binders, 1 difference, #13 hC : C.CausallyArcConnected -> harc. alexandrovTopology_eq_lift: 20 binders, 1 difference at #13. stronglyCausalOpen_lift: 19 binders, 1 difference at #13. stronglyCausal_lift_of_weakMorphism: 19 binders, 1 difference at #13. stronglyCausal_lift_self: 17 binders, 1 difference at #11. Conclusions are identical. Under pp.explicit, harc's type equals the harc binder of mem_connectedComponentIn_diamond_of_curves (Causal/StrongCausalityLifts.lean:284) and of le_top_map_of_curves (:303). The originals use hC only through CausallyArcConnected.exists_causalCurveOn_top (:276; see :345, :371), so harc is exactly what their proofs consume. The five examples (:167-190) are typed by type_of% of the originals. Each proves its original from the new form plus exists_causalCurveOn_top, never from the original itself, so they are non-trivial and kernel-checked at elaboration. harc is the target's hypothesis (≤ at ⊤ realised by causal curves of ⊤ over [0, 1]).

labels.label: item (2): not_stronglyCausal_lift_of_curves_glued (:330)
labels.notes: Read through forallTelescope on type.appArg! with pp.explicit, tracking which of the two topologies on N each binder mentions (binder #3 = τc, #4 = the anonymous instance). C : @Causality N inst. The three ∀ W, AbsolutelyMinimalOn W (for C, CM and CX, binders #12-14) and Continuous p, Continuous D (#15, #16) all sit inside the negated ∀ and use the instances. τc occurs only in #17 (inst ≤ τc) and #22 (@connectedComponentIn N τc). The conclusion @StronglyCausal N inst C does not mention τc. Pretty-printed binder diff against not_stronglyCausal_lift_of_curves (StrongCausalityLifts.lean:649): exactly the five added binders, nothing removed or altered. Adding hypotheses inside a negated ∀ strengthens the refutation, so this refutes the printed form a fortiori, with the curve hypothesis in its strongest reading (every U, U', every segment). Universe 0, like the parent. Witness: symmRationalLine is absolutely minimal on every open set (symmRationalLine_absolutelyMinimalOn). The timelike line is too, via CausallyArcConnected.absolutelyMinimalOn_all (GXStructure.lean:496) on timelikeLine_causallyArcConnected. id is continuous (continuous_id in ℝ's topology), and τc = ℝ's topology with le_rfl. F1's sentence 'the refutation says nothing about a causal or tarentin M̃' is accurate: the witness is ¬IsCausal (:274) and ¬Tarentin (:280), proved and conjoined at :305. It also fails harc (:287), the one hypothesis of the harc form it misses. The glued refutation covers the strong-causality conclusion only. The with-tarentin (Alexandrov) conclusion is not refuted under gluing, which the SCOPE's 'says nothing about a ... tarentin N' implicitly discloses.

labels.label: extra: orderLine_strongCausalityLift_of_le_realised (:252)
labels.notes: orderLine is Causal/Morphism.lean:804 (x ≤_U y iff x ≤ y ∧ x ∈ U ∧ y ∈ U). It is not causally arc-connected: 0 ≤ 2 in U = ℝ∖{1}, and a curve of U would take the value 1 by the intermediate value theorem (:233). That is correct: the relation does not require [x, y] ⊆ U. harc holds by the segment (:221). 'Not absolutely minimal' is true: GluingModels.orderLine_not_minimal (NonMinimal.lean:191). It is disclosed in three places: as a conjunct of the statement itself, in its docstring ('a witness of the no-gluing reading only'), and in the module docstring and SCOPE (:37, :59-60). The module's 'Strictly weaker than arc-connectedness' (:35) holds over all causalities (CAC ⇒ harc via :276, and orderLine shows the converse fails) and is qualified for gluing at :37 and :59.

findings.what: 'it implies the `M`-only form' uses OQ-95's term, gluing as AbsolutelyMinimal on the whole space. In this file, though, M names the codomain of p, so the phrase reads as 'gluing of M alone'. The mathematics is right: GluingModels.absolutelyMinimal_of_forall turns hereditary gluing into whole-space absolute minimality, so the refutation covers that reading too.
